topic: Decoding Epidemics: The SIR Model Mechanics
target_audience: University students (Introductory Epidemiology or System Dynamics)

sections.title: The Core Concept: Defining Populations
lecture_lines: Epidemics are modeled by three population states.
Infectious (I) are currently carrying the virus.
Total population N equals S plus I plus R.
animations: Create a visual box for S (Susceptible) in #FFD700.
Show an arrow from S to I representing transmission.
Show an arrow from I to R representing recovery.

sections.title: The Dynamics of Transmission (The Math of Interaction)
lecture_lines: Transmission rate beta drives new infections.
Infection happens through contact between Susceptible and Infectious.
Higher beta means faster disease spread.
animations: Animate particles moving between S and I.
Show interaction frequency with a pulsing #FFFFFF glow.
Display transmission rate parameter 'beta' near the arrow.

sections.title: The Recovery Mechanism (The Gamma Factor)
lecture_lines: Gamma represents the rate of recovery.
Infected individuals transition to the Recovered state.
The infectious period ends as Gamma takes effect.
animations: Highlight the I to R transition clearly.
Display the recovery rate parameter 'gamma' in #00CED1.
Show the decrease in Infectious count over time.

sections.title: Visualizing the Curves
lecture_lines: The SIR model plots state changes over time.
The Infectious curve peaks at the epidemic height.
Susceptible population steadily declines over time.
Recovered population grows as individuals gain immunity.
The curves illustrate herd immunity evolution.
animations: Draw a graph with time on x-axis, count on y-axis.
Plot the S curve in #FFD700 decaying over time.
Plot the I curve in #FF4500 peaking then falling.

sections.title: Application: The Power of Intervention
lecture_lines: Lowering transmission rates flattens the infectious curve.
Models guide critical public health policies.
animations: Show a line representing intervention lowering the peak.
Compare original peak height with reduced peak height.
Display the flattened curve in #32CD32 clearly.
